body: Forward test of the valuation-temperature method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.42 (naive base rate 0.48) that: Hindalco's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return. Evidence: Yahoo/screener 20-Nov-2026: Hindalco ₹929.5 (52-wk ₹772–1,179); Nifty 50 25,800.6. Screener: P/E 8.97 on TTM EPS ₹85.4, P/B ~1.3, market cap ₹2.09 lakh cr; but earnings are at a cyclical peak: quarterly OP ₹13,932 cr (Jun-26) and ₹12,814 cr (Sep-26) vs ₹7,500–10,000 cr in the prior eight quarters; H1 FY27 EPS ₹64.7 (≈₹130 annualised). Q2 FY27 call (12-Nov-2026): record copper EBITDA ₹1,673 cr on 'elevated LME prices'; aluminium hedged only ~29% of rest-of-FY27 at $3,000/t; Novelis EBITDA/t $289 in Q2 vs $600 long-term guide, Oswego normalised, Bay Minette commercial shipments slipped to Q1 FY28; net debt/EBITDA 1.8×; ₹50,000 cr India capex programme. Reasoning: Valuation-temperature with a cyclical twist: the stock is 'cold' on P/E but that P/E is computed on peak commodity earnings with mostly unhedged LME exposure. The classic pattern (low P/E at the top of the cycle) argues slightly against outperformance; offset by Novelis recovery optionality. Resolution: YES if (Hindalco NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 929.5) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored. Source: NSE / Yahoo Finance closes (HINDALCO.NS, ^NSEI). Resolve by 2027-06-30; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: A single Nifty-50 large cap beats the index over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%).
data.resolution_rule: YES if (Hindalco NSE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 929.5) > (Nifty 50 close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 25,800.6). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits/bonuses; dividends ignored.

title: Paper call: Hindalco's share price return from 20-Nov-2026 to 30-Jun-2027 beats the Nifty 50's price return
